experiment_description: A four-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometer was implemented on a 16-qubit frequency-tunable transmon superconducting processor. The interferometer used Q0 as the input/first beam splitter, Q1 as path 1, Q2 as path 2 and which-way detector, and Q3 as the second beam splitter/output. Relevant nearest-neighbor photon-hopping rates were J_Q0Q1/2π = 3.49 MHz, J_Q0Q2/2π = 3.56 MHz, J_Q1Q3/2π = 3.86 MHz, and J_Q2Q3/2π = 3.41 MHz. After initial readout post-selection of all qubits in |0>, a microwave photon was generated by a π pulse on Q0. Q0, Q1, and Q2 were tuned to the common working frequency 5.82 GHz for 57 ns so the excitation split into Q1 and Q2. The qubits were then detuned to freeze hopping: Q0 was placed at its idle frequency, Q2 remained at 5.82 GHz, and Q1 was placed at the waiting frequency 5.83 GHz. A 100 ns dispersive readout pulse of variable amplitude was applied to Q2, followed by a resonator-decay wait, producing an average measurement-induced dephasing rate Γ_m calibrated over the 200 ns measurement interval. Γ_m/2π was swept from no which-way measurement to the strong-measurement regime, with representative interference-fringe traces taken at Γ_m/2π = 0, 0.333, 0.748, 1.330, and 2.365 MHz; the calibration extended to about 3.695 MHz. A phase was then accumulated on path 1 by biasing Q1 to 5.83 GHz + δ/2π for t_p = 100 ns, with δ/2π swept from 0 to 30 MHz, corresponding to phase φ = -t_p δ. Finally Q1, Q2, and Q3 were tuned to 5.82 GHz for 49 ns and Q3 was measured. The interference visibility was extracted from the measured Q3 excited-state population P_I versus δ using V = (P_I,max - P_I,min)/(P_I,max + P_I,min).

visibility_at_gamma_over_2pi_0_MHz.description: Approximate fringe visibility of the Q3 population oscillation with no which-way measurement-induced dephasing.

visibility_at_gamma_over_2pi_0_333_MHz.description: Approximate fringe visibility of the Q3 population oscillation for a weak Q2 which-way measurement.

visibility_at_gamma_over_2pi_0_748_MHz.description: Approximate fringe visibility of the Q3 population oscillation for an intermediate Q2 which-way measurement.

visibility_at_gamma_over_2pi_1_330_MHz.description: Approximate fringe visibility of the Q3 population oscillation for a stronger Q2 which-way measurement.

visibility_at_gamma_over_2pi_2_365_MHz.description: Approximate fringe visibility of the Q3 population oscillation for a near-projective Q2 which-way measurement.

visibility_high_dephasing_limit.description: Observed limiting fringe visibility as the which-way measurement strength approached the projective regime in the four-qubit interferometer.

experiment_description: A two-qubit quantum-state tomography experiment was performed on the two arms of the same four-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometer. The processor, connectivity, and first splitting stage were the same as in the four-qubit interference experiment: all qubits were post-selected in |0>, Q0 was excited, and Q0, Q1, and Q2 were tuned to 5.82 GHz for 57 ns so the photon occupied the two paths Q1 and Q2. The qubits were then detuned to freeze hopping, with Q0 at idle, Q2 at 5.82 GHz, and Q1 at 5.83 GHz. A 100 ns dispersive which-way measurement pulse was applied to Q2 and the resonator was allowed to decay; the average measurement-induced dephasing rate Γ_m/2π was varied from 0 to about 3.695 MHz using the calibrated readout-pulse amplitude. Unlike the interference experiment, no phase-accumulation pulse and no Q1–Q2–Q3 final beam-splitter evolution were applied. Instead, after an additional wait, two-qubit state tomography was performed on Q1 and Q2. From the reconstructed density matrix ρ_Q1Q2, the Wootters concurrence C_Q1Q2 was computed. The density matrix was also projected into the single-excitation subspace spanned by |10> and |01> using P = |10><10| + |01><01| and normalized as ρ_s = P ρ_Q1Q2 P / Tr(P ρ_Q1Q2). The single-excitation purity was P_s = Tr(ρ_s^2), and the single-excitation von Neumann entropy was S_s = -Tr(ρ_s log2 ρ_s).

concurrence_at_zero_dephasing.description: Measured two-qubit concurrence between Q1 and Q2 after the first beam splitter when no which-way dephasing was applied.

concurrence_strong_dephasing_limit.description: Measured limiting two-qubit concurrence between Q1 and Q2 under strong which-way measurement-induced dephasing.

single_excitation_purity_strong_dephasin.description: Approximate limiting purity of the Q1–Q2 single-excitation density matrix under strong which-way measurement-induced dephasing.

single_excitation_entropy_strong_dephasi.description: Approximate limiting von Neumann entropy of the Q1–Q2 single-excitation density matrix under strong which-way measurement-induced dephasing.

purity_vs_dephasing_trend.description: Observed dependence of the single-excitation purity on the which-way measurement-induced dephasing rate in the four-qubit interferometer.

entropy_vs_dephasing_trend.description: Observed dependence of the single-excitation von Neumann entropy on the which-way measurement-induced dephasing rate in the four-qubit interferometer.

experiment_description: A twelve-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometer was implemented on the same 16-qubit frequency-tunable transmon processor. A single photon was generated by exciting Q0 after initial post-selection in |0>. All 12 interferometer qubits were tuned to the working frequency 5.82 GHz and evolved for up to 200 ns. The first beam splitter was Q0. Path 1 was Q1–Q4–Q5–Q7–Q13 and then Q15; the relevant hopping rates were J_Q0Q1/2π = 3.49 MHz, J_Q1Q4/2π = 4.65 MHz, J_Q4Q5/2π = 3.29 MHz, J_Q5Q7/2π = 4.00 MHz, J_Q7Q13/2π = 4.14 MHz, and J_Q13Q15/2π = 4.11 MHz. Path 2 was Q2–Q8–Q10–Q11–Q14 and then Q15; the relevant hopping rates were J_Q0Q2/2π = 3.56 MHz, J_Q2Q8/2π = 4.94 MHz, J_Q8Q10/2π = 3.40 MHz, J_Q10Q11/2π = 3.45 MHz, J_Q11Q14/2π = 4.47 MHz, and J_Q14Q15/2π = 3.49 MHz. Q2 served as the continuously monitored which-way detector. A continuous readout-frequency pulse was applied to Q2 before initial state preparation and maintained throughout the 12-qubit evolution; its Stark shift was compensated by the Q2 Z-bias pulse. The Q2 measurement-induced dephasing rate Γ_m was calibrated by Stark-shift measurements, and representative population-evolution maps were acquired at Γ_m/2π = 0, 5.921, 11.195, and 18.134 MHz. Population of every qubit was measured as a function of evolution time to track propagation and interference at Q15.

quantum_zeno_path_blocking_observed.description: Whether continuous which-way measurement of Q2 produced measurement-induced blocking/reflection of the path containing Q2.

propagation_trend_with_increasing_dephas.description: Observed change in single-photon propagation through the twelve-qubit interferometer as the Q2 continuous which-way measurement strength was increased.

experiment_description: A two-qubit tomography experiment was performed inside the twelve-qubit continuously monitored Mach–Zehnder interferometer to quantify information leakage and entanglement between the two arms. The same twelve-qubit paths and continuous Q2 which-way measurement protocol were used as in the twelve-qubit population-evolution experiment: all interferometer qubits were tuned to 5.82 GHz, Q0 was initially excited, Q2 was continuously measured with Stark-shift compensation, and Γ_m/2π was swept from zero to the strong-measurement regime extending beyond 20 MHz. At the evolution time for which the Q4–Q8 concurrence reached its maximum in the absence of which-way measurement, two-qubit state tomography was performed on Q4 and Q8, which lie in opposite arms after the first splitting stage. From the reconstructed ρ_Q4Q8, the Wootters concurrence C_Q4Q8 was computed. The state was also projected into the single-excitation subspace spanned by |10> and |01>, normalized to ρ_s, and used to compute P_s = Tr(ρ_s^2) and S_s = -Tr(ρ_s log2 ρ_s).

concurrence_at_zero_dephasing.description: Approximate Q4–Q8 concurrence at the tomography time without continuous which-way measurement-induced dephasing.

concurrence_at_high_dephasing.description: Approximate Q4–Q8 concurrence at high continuous which-way measurement-induced dephasing near the upper end of the experimental sweep.

single_excitation_purity_minimum.description: Approximate minimum measured single-excitation purity of the Q4–Q8 subsystem as Γ_m was swept.

single_excitation_purity_minimum_gamma_o.description: Approximate dephasing-rate location of the minimum in Q4–Q8 single-excitation purity during the continuous-measurement sweep.

single_excitation_entropy_maximum_bits.description: Approximate maximum measured single-excitation von Neumann entropy of the Q4–Q8 subsystem as Γ_m was swept.

single_excitation_entropy_maximum_gamma_.description: Approximate dephasing-rate location of the maximum in Q4–Q8 single-excitation von Neumann entropy during the continuous-measurement sweep.

purity_vs_dephasing_trend.description: Observed dependence of Q4–Q8 single-excitation purity on continuous which-way measurement-induced dephasing in the twelve-qubit interferometer.

entropy_vs_dephasing_trend.description: Observed dependence of Q4–Q8 single-excitation von Neumann entropy on continuous which-way measurement-induced dephasing in the twelve-qubit interferometer.
